note: Curated, balanced accounts. Refreshed by the daily 7am routine via the X connector.

posts.name: Nate Silver
posts.text: Pretty insane agreement between prediction markets and final FLIPR forecasts. They're more bullish on Ds in AK and MS, more bearish in some states where there have been historical polling errors (and the Stevens/AES thing in MI). But the average state is only 3 points different.

posts.name: G. Elliott Morris
posts.text: No sign yet of the Election Day surge in turnout Republicans need to meet their 2024 or 2022 turnout patterns. But it's early, and will have much better picture in a few hours.

posts.name: G. Elliott Morris
posts.text: Look it's early and just one state, but I'm not seeing anything indicating that the inference from early voting, that GOP turnout is way down, isn't applying to Election Day voters as well.

posts.name: Cook Political Report
posts.text: Our new range of potential Democratic pickups moves to three to six seats, still giving Republicans a small chance to hold the majority if our Toss Ups break their way, but we ultimately view a Democratic majority as the likelier scenario.

posts.name: Decision Desk HQ
posts.text: Polling roundup (11/3): As of Election Day, Democrats lead the generic ballot by 8.6% in the DDHQ polling average. President Trump's approval rating is underwater by over 20 percentage points.

posts.name: Sean Trende
posts.text: This is why the swing of suburbs in major metro areas in the Trump era away from the GOP has had such an outsized impact in Texas.

posts.name: Matthew Yglesias
posts.text: Even a very Republican-skewing judicial branch has been a meaningful check on Trump, and flipping the Senate, and only flipping the Senate, stops Trump from stacking the judiciary.

posts.name: Aaron Rupar
posts.text: Energy Secretary Chris Wright: "Prices are high. The best cure for high prices is high prices. It grows supply."

posts.name: Matthew Yglesias
posts.text: The Free Press never actually does anything to praise pro-Israel Democrats; the Michigan outcome where they lose primaries and switch parties is the whole goal of the enterprise.

posts.name: Byron York
posts.text: In the primary, Abdul el Sayed's lead turned out to be 1/10 the size the polls said it was, but he still won. After Tuesday, he'll either be the next senator from Michigan or a new case study in partisan nonresponse bias.

posts.name: Erick Erickson
posts.text: In the mid-nineties, George W. Bush and Karl Rove ended 100 years of Democrat rule in Texas. Today they are anathema to the current Texas GOP. We'll see if today's Texas GOP can do what those guys did and keep the Democrats out of power.

posts.name: Guy Benson
posts.text: Caveats galore, and remember that FL Republicans blew the doors off in 2022 and that statewide red wave did not translate nationwide. But the FL GOP ticket must be pleased to see this, so far. And the main lesson applies everywhere: vote!

posts.name: Erick Erickson
posts.text: For two years the MAGA mantra in DC has been, "We can just do things." Today, voters will say loudly that they can just do things too.

posts.name: Axios
posts.text: Final polls, models and markets see a "blue tsunami"

posts.name: CNN Politics
posts.text: The balance of power in Washington is at stake as Americans vote to determine control of the Senate and House, plus races for governor. See our guide to poll closing times and when to expect results.

posts.name: POLITICO
posts.text: BREAKING: The Justice Department is asking the Supreme Court for an emergency order forcing California to set aside ballots cast by 20,000 registered voters the Trump administration claims are likely noncitizens.
